How login works

how does login work in this project?

Step 1 of 4auth.ts

Steps

Glossary

handleLogin
The entry point of login: it takes an email and password and returns either a failure reason or a new session.
passwordHash
The stored, hashed form of a user's password. The login never compares plain passwords, only hashes.
verifyPassword
Hashes the submitted password and checks whether it equals the stored hash.
startSession
Creates a session object with the user id, a start timestamp and a random token after a successful login.
findUser
Looks up a user by email. Here it searches a hard-coded in-memory array.
⌃⌥ ← →
How login works
Tour map · 4 steps

How login works

how does login work in this project?

Login is driven by handleLogin: it looks up the user by email, verifies the password against the stored hash, and on success issues a session. If the user is missing or the password is wrong, it returns a generic failure reason instead.

Step 2 of 5auth.ts

Path

    1. Inside handleLogin

Steps

Glossary

passwordHash
Field on the user record from findUser; passed to verifyPassword, never compared as plain text.
hashPassword
Private helper in password.ts that transforms the submitted password before comparison.
short-circuit
JavaScript || skips the right side when the left is true; here it skips verifyPassword when user is undefined.
userId
The user.id string from findUser; the only argument startSession receives from handleLogin.

Step 1 of 4auth.ts:4–10

The login entry point

handleLoginThe entry point of login: it takes an email and password and returns either a failure reason or a new session. is where login begins. It finds the user by email, rejects the attempt if the user is missing or the password is wrong, and otherwise returns a new session.

  • Low · Breaks on changeline 6

    verifyPasswordHashes the submitted password and checks whether it equals the stored hash. returns a boolean synchronously; this guard relies on that (no await). If verifyPassword became async the ! would always be false and the guard would silently pass.

Why return a result object instead of throwing an error?

A wrong email or password is an expected outcome, not a crash. handleLoginThe entry point of login: it takes an email and password and returns either a failure reason or a new session. returns { ok: false, reason } so the caller can show the message without a try/catch, and both failures share one reason, so an attacker cannot tell which part was wrong ().

The guard before any session
